races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Fillies Maiden
Champion Lettings Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Wicklow Gap
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse that fades in finishes, with three recent runs at 7f on Standside going and limited turf form; the mile trip and Good ground are fine on paper but a tendency to fade and traffic risk in this congested field are real concerns.

runners_data.name: Nosmokewithoutfire
runners_data.note: Apprentice-ridden hold-up type returning from 37 days off, with very limited sim-going form (1/3) and a habit of fading; a 12-furlong stamina run on last start suggests the mile is sharp enough, but the finishing pattern is worrying here.

runners_data.name: Dream Legend
runners_data.note: Ran well to win over 8f on Soft ground and has a recent win on his CV; 71 days off is a query, but Leigh Roche retains the ride and the mile trip suits — a hold-up runner who will need a clean run in a very crowded finish.

runners_data.name: Enthusiastically
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes takes over on a horse rated at its best when finishing 4th-4th-4th at 7f on Standside ground; the step up to a mile on Good turf is the unknown, but the horse has shown consistent prominentish speed without winning and could slot into a position just off the early leader.

runners_data.name: Fontaine Khaled
runners_data.note: Apprentice Jessica O'Gorman aboard; the horse has placed once on Good ground and shown form at 7f on Good — step up to a mile is the key question, and the fading-in-finish flag is a concern, but Good going suits and she has recent competitive form at this level.

runners_data.name: Caoilte
runners_data.note: David Marnane's runner carries the tongue-tie and has raced at 7-8f repeatedly without threatening; a true hold-up horse who will find himself unable to secure his natural rearward position in this field — the STYLE_FIT tag tempers expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes a notable booking on a horse that has raced four times all on Good ground (4/4 sim-going runs) — the strongest going match in the field; despite being a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map, Keane's navigation could matter if a gap materialises.

runners_data.name: Hugo Spritz
runners_data.note: Has the hood noted in headgear and ran 9th on last start just 13 days ago; a true hold-up type with a fading tendency who will be racing out of his natural role in this crowded shape, and very limited form makes it hard to identify an angle.

runners_data.name: Stonyfalls
runners_data.note: Returns quickly (13 days) for Paul Traynor with a modest record; a consistent mid-teen finisher who is a natural hold-up horse shuffled into midfield on the map — four recent runs on Good going are a positive but the form figures offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, trained by Michael Mulvany with a decent 14-day strike rate; stepped back from 9-10f trips to a mile, with three of five recent runs on Good ground — uniquely positioned to control this race from the front without a rival to challenge him.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon
runners_data.note: McCourt's second string alongside Nosmokewithoutfire; a true hold-up horse with the widest range of finishing positions (2nd to 13th) and a fading flag — has to find a run from the rear in a packed field, which is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness runner with a recent placed run (4th) and a win on Standside; a genuine hold-up type who will be hard-pressed to find clear air from a congested rear group, with the STYLE_FIT note suggesting his natural position is compromised in this race.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Mulvany's second runner alongside Borora Aura, with Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) aboard; has placed twice in recent form (5th, 4th) on Good ground and the tongue/bit headgear suggests he needs assistance — a true hold-up horse crammed into midfield, but the claim is a marginal positive.

runners_data.name: Threebiggulps
runners_data.note: Hood-wearing hold-up type with four consecutive single-figure finishes and a fading tendency; 31 days since last run and limited form on Good ground make him a tough ride for Nathan Crosse in a field this congested.

runners_data.name: Wedding Year
runners_data.note: Bit-and-tongue headgear, two recent runs just 10 days apart for Adrian McGuinness; has shown a 3rd and 4th place finish recently, suggesting some residual form — a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield, and the quick turnaround bears watching for trainer intent.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes over on Slattery's runner, fresh from 8 days ago; all recent form is at 5-6f (including a 21st last time), so stepping up to a mile on Good is a significant trip test — a natural hold-up horse out of his comfort zone in distance as well as race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Borora Aura is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and, crucially, faces no meaningful pressure for the lead — she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this flat Bellewstown mile without being harassed. Behind her, the overwhelming majority of the field are genuine hold-up horses, but with so many closers competing for the same ground, the midfield and rear will be congested and traffic-laden, making clean runs hard to find late. Sayonara, Caoilte, Due In June, Beau Army, Cause I Like You, Wedding Year and several others are all true hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map simply because there is not enough rear-guard space for them all — in reality, they will bunch and obstruct each other. This pace shape — one uncontested leader, a sustainable tempo, and a packed, traffic-dense chasing group — squarely favours horses with prominent racing speed who can track Borora Aura at close quarters and produce their challenge without being trapped in a wall of horses.

scenarios.body: If a horse tracking just off Borora Aura's shoulder in clear air produces a smooth, unimpeded challenge from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Threads Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is stronger than expected and a hold-up horse finds a fortunate gap to deliver a late surge.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is stronger than expected and a hold-up horse finds a fortunate gap to deliver a late surge.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Borora Aura sets an unusually slow early pace and the whole field is compressed into a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Borora Aura (front-runner) is the only horse guaranteed a clear, unimpeded run — monitor how quickly she establishes a lead and whether the pace she sets is genuinely slow enough to allow closers to reel her in.

Due In June holds four consecutive runs on Good ground (sim-going 4/4) and Colin Keane's booking is the most significant jockey upgrade in the race — watch whether Keane manoeuvres him into a better position than his hold-up tag suggests.

The congested hold-up cluster — Caoilte, Beau Army, Cause I Like You, Wedding Year and Threebiggulps — will all be competing for the same inside rail gaps from two furlongs out; a single horse finding a seam could change the result sharply.

Enthusiastically has finished 4th-4th-4th in recent starts and Chris Hayes may try to take advantage of the uncontested pace by sitting just behind Borora Aura — if he can hold that prominent pitch, the horse's consistent near-miss form becomes relevant.

Fontaine Khaled is stepping from 6-7f to a mile for the first time; if the trip is within her compass on Good ground, her placed form at this level gives her a live each-way chance in the prominent-tracking scenario.

races.name: Ploughman Bar And Grill Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: Bellewstown-trained hold-up specialist for T G McCourt, back after 20 days and steps back in trip to 1m on Good going where he has placed twice in 15 similar-ground runs; likely to be further back than ideal in this crowded field.

runners_data.name: Wellwhatshappenin
runners_data.note: Returns after 104 days off for the Harty yard — the long break is the key concern here; hold-up style and a tendency to fade in the finish makes a first-time-back effort in a compressed 18-runner field a significant ask on quick ground.

runners_data.name: Carvalhal
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race, Burns can steal the initiative unchallenged; recent form shows a win and place at this sort of mark, though the STYLE_FIT flag notes this horse is stepping slightly out of role, so a dominant display rather than a grinding one is needed.

runners_data.name: Rockbury Lad
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-tie and has placed twice in 15 similar-going outings including a win; hold-up type who at 14 days returns to action for O'Callaghan but needs a stronger pace than Carvalhal alone is likely to generate over the mile.

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: Wears hood and hasn't run in 59 days for Duffy; races from hold-up, has placed twice from behind at 7f-8f on Soft/Standard, but zero wins on Good and the extended absence makes this a tough reintroduction in a crowded handicap.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a genuine win and five places over 6f-8f on Good — very much in his element here; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is a useful bonus and this horse's style is a natural fit for a controlled single-pace race that rewards those in the front half.

runners_data.name: Captain Ciano
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose last five runs have all come over 10f — dropping back to 1m is a distance query on top of the style redistribution; the McCourt yard is in reasonable form but STYLE_FIT and trip doubts combine to make this a speculative price play.

runners_data.name: Secret Magician
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has finished 3rd over 8f on Good ground; genuinely a hold-up horse shunted into a midfield slot by the crowded rear — Hassett's charge has done enough at this level to make him dangerous if he finds daylight, but the redistribution means he won't get his natural rhythm.

runners_data.name: Virgil Tibbs
runners_data.note: 239 days off the track is the glaring concern for McConnell; fades in the finish and all five recent runs have been 8f-10f on Soft/Standard — the step up to Good ground after that absence makes this a risky proposition.

runners_data.name: Tortola
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old back after 139 days for Slattery; bred to want further than 1m and all five recent runs have been on Standard or Soft, so the Good ground today is an untested variable compounding the layoff.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-tie and visor for the McCourt yard; genuine prominent runner who is the second-most natural fit for this pace shape alongside Carvalhal, but a record of 0 wins and 1 place from 15 Good-ground runs raises questions about whether he can convert.

runners_data.name: Pinball Wizard
runners_data.note: Wears hood and has placed twice over 8f on Good, both coming from hold-up; shunted into a midfield slot because the rear is oversubscribed — McConnell's veteran struggles to operate out of his comfort zone, so getting a clean passage is everything.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: A two-year-old carrying big weight and not seen for 261 days — Seamie Heffernan's presence is the one compelling angle, but the combination of the long break, age, trip and redistribution from the rear make this a very difficult selection to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Plastic Paddy
runners_data.note: Back after 202 days, fades in finish, and two of the last five starts were over extreme distances (17f, 24f) — the drop to 1m and return from a long break are both strikes, and the redistribution out of a hold-up berth compounds the negatives.

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Wears hood and has placed over 7f-8f on Standard for McCourt; returns 14 days after last run which keeps it fresh, and a string of placed efforts (2-3-2-3 recently) shows consistency, though Good ground is an untested element and the redistribution from the rear limits the chance.

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-tie and headgear; placed four times in 15 similar-going runs but never won, and all recent placing came on Standard — Good ground today is unproven, and 52 days since last run is not a major concern but the form trajectory offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Shelbourne Flyer
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's hold-up type has placed twice on Good ground at 7f and ran 3rd at Bellewstown over 7f — the course form is the standout angle here; pushed into midfield on the map by the congested rear, but if Meade's runners are in form (T14: 1/18) and the horse can sit forward enough, this is one of the stronger redistributed profiles.

runners_data.name: Hastily
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and has returned just 13th, 14th, 15th and 16th in the last four runs — McGuinness's runner has not won on Good in 15 attempts over this trip and there is nothing in the recent form to suggest this changes today.

races.paceDynamic: Carvalhal is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 0-60 handicap over a mile at Bellewstown, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Nicola Burns can dictate a controlled, even pace from the front without being pressed or harassed at any stage. The prominent types — Dinamine and Rampage — will likely sit just off the leader's shoulder, creating an organised and unhurried early gallop that gives nothing away for free from behind. On Good ground at a flat course with a sustainable tempo set by one uncontested leader, horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and produce a sustained finish from the two-furlong pole will be ideally positioned — deep closers who need a strong pace to reel rivals in will find the fractions insufficient to close the gap from far back. This shape strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield profile: runners who can sit within three or four lengths of Carvalhal, conserve energy through an honest but unrushed mile, and unleash a clean finish from the front half of the field. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically get to the rear in a natural shape — Shelbourne Flyer, Secret Magician, Captain Ciano, Pinball Wizard and several others have been redistributed to midfield on the map; of these, Shelbourne Flyer and Secret Magician have the class and course form most likely to allow them to at least secure a forward midfield berth if they miss their natural position.

scenarios.title: Carvalhal Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Carvalhal bowls along uncontested and sets a controlled, even pace that suits those racing in the first half of the field.
scenarios.body: If Carvalhal bowls along uncontested and sets a controlled, even pace that suits those racing in the first half of the field.

scenarios.title: Midfield Surge, Class Prevails

scenarios.body: If the even tempo compresses the field and a well-placed midfield runner picks the right moment to quicken past a tiring front group.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively quick with several prominent runners over-committing and setting up a genuine rattle home.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves deceptively quick with several prominent runners over-committing and setting up a genuine rattle home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gifts It
scenarios.trigger: If Carvalhal is left alone in front and simply never relinquishes the advantage, making all on a career-best effort at this mark.
scenarios.body: If Carvalhal is left alone in front and simply never relinquishes the advantage, making all on a career-best effort at this mark.

watchPoints.text: Carvalhal ridden by Nicola Burns (5lb claim) must be tracked from the off — if she bowls along unchallenged and the first-quarter fractions are modest, every horse behind her will be in a race that suits her and she becomes extremely dangerous in a scenario where no one is willing to go and get her.

Dinamine and Rampage are both genuine prominent types and will compete for the same early position just off Carvalhal — if they race too keenly for that ground in an 18-runner field, both could use excess energy in the first half-mile and their finishing efforts may be compromised.

Shelbourne Flyer has the best Good-ground course profile among the redistributed hold-up horses and Meade will have a clear tactical plan — watch for any sign of this horse being produced on the inner on the home turn, as it has the form to make a mid-race move count.

With 18 runners on a flat turning mile, traffic and position at the turn for home will be critical — horses drawn wide or forced to race three-wide throughout are at a meaningful disadvantage regardless of style, and this is a race where the draw and early positioning should be noted at flag-fall.

Several runners return from significant absences (Micasso 261 days, Virgil Tibbs 239 days, Plastic Paddy 202 days) — if any of these market-drifters are backed late, track any stable confidence signal, but their form profile and fitness queries make them lower-order prospects on the available evidence.

races.name: Indaver Ireland Handicap

runners_data.name: Billie Be Quick
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for Mrs Harrington and Shane Foley who needs pace to close into; 12 days since last run is a positive freshness angle, but similar-going figures of only 1 win from 15 are modest and this course/trip profile is tight for a pure closer off a likely steady gallop.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here with Colin Keane in the saddle, her form reads 221-80 suggesting recent softening but she has won off this mark and her natural style suits the likely race shape; 27 days since last run is manageable and the style-fit note means she is operating exactly in role, the key departure point for everything else in the race.

runners_data.name: Namiid
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners a horse with a genuinely strong five-furlong record on Good ground — winning and placing consistently — and J P Murtagh's yard is in decent form at 1 from 21 over 14 days; a natural prominent racer who should slot behind Rosie Frith cleanly, making this the most style-aligned threat to the leader.

runners_data.name: Smoke Them Out
runners_data.note: A hold-up type dropping back from seven furlongs to five for McCourt, with only 6 days between runs and most of the historical form coming on Heavier surfaces; the similar-going record of 0 wins from 6 on comparable going is a concern and the step down in trip adds uncertainty for a horse used to settling over further.

runners_data.name: Sporting Hero
runners_data.note: Durkan's six-year-old has a genuine win on Good ground over five furlongs and is a natural front-runner by inclination, but with Rosie Frith already owning the lead, he is unlikely to reproduce that winning shape here; the visor headgear suggests he needs restraining, and his wider market price reflects the difficulty of getting his position.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Cromwell's three-year-old ran only yesterday — a very short turnaround that must be flagged — and while her prominent style would normally see her racing handily, she is one of several horses naturally inclined toward the front who cannot all occupy that ground; consistent placed form but the 1-day break and positional squeeze make her profile harder to assess confidently.

races.paceDynamic: Rosie Frith is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a six-runner field over five furlongs at Bellewstown, she should secure a clean lead without being pressured and set a controlled, sustainable gallop. Colin Keane aboard a horse who has shown a clear pattern of leading or racing close to the pace means the tempo is unlikely to be frenetic, creating a race that rewards those who can track closely and quicken from a handy position rather than those coming from deep. Namiid and the redistributed Sporting Hero and Treasured Royal are all naturally prominent types, but with Rosie Frith already occupying the lead, only one or two of them can genuinely slot in behind — most likely Namiid given Ben Coen's experience managing prominent horses and Namiid's consistent record of racing close to the pace on Good ground. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all access those forward positions, with Rosie Frith most certain to lead and Namiid best placed to sit second, leaving Sporting Hero and Treasured Royal likely to be shuffled back against their natural inclinations. This race shape squarely favours a confirmed prominent racer or a close tracker who can quicken off a measured gallop — a true hold-up horse needing a strong pace to close into is disadvantaged here.

scenarios.title: Rosie Frith Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rosie Frith secures an uncontested lead and dictates a measured, sustainable tempo throughout the five furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Rosie Frith secures an uncontested lead and dictates a measured, sustainable tempo throughout the five furlongs.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough early to string the field out and leave a gap for a late finisher from behind.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough early to string the field out and leave a gap for a late finisher from behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Scramble Muddies Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Sporting Hero or Treasured Royal push forward aggressively early and create an unexpectedly contested pace.
scenarios.body: If Sporting Hero or Treasured Royal push forward aggressively early and create an unexpectedly contested pace.

watchPoints.text: Rosie Frith — if Colin Keane elects to push forward assertively from the gates and gets a clear, uncontested lead, the entire race shape locks into the dominant scenario and all other runners are chasing a potentially gone-away leader.

Sporting Hero and Treasured Royal — if either pushes hard for position in the early stages against their mapped role, the resulting pace scramble could compress the field and neutralise Rosie Frith's tactical advantage entirely.
Treasured Royal — ran only 1 day ago; monitor in the market for any sign of trainer-confidence withdrawal or market drift that would signal a precautionary run rather than a winning visit.

Namiid — watch where Ben Coen positions him out of the gates; if he slots smoothly into second behind Rosie Frith without burning energy, his five-furlong Good-ground record makes him the most dangerous rival in the expected race shape.

Billie Be Quick — Shane Foley will need an unusually strong pace from the front to get a clear run at them from hold-up; if the first two furlongs look slow in running, this one's chance diminishes quickly and any strong move early from her position should be treated with caution.

races.name: McNallys Pharmacy Apprentice Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Kevin The Great
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for Gavin Cromwell who has placed over 10f on good and Healy ground, but this 13f trip on good going produced only a fourth last time — strong claims on similar form but must overcome a tendency to come from too far back in a potentially slowly run race.

runners_data.name: Desert Friend
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran who won over 14f on soft last time and handles good ground, though his two runs over 13f on good have yielded a 12th and a 9th — genuine stamina but his best form may require cut in the ground.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner, she won over 13f at Bellewstown on good and placed over 16f on good, giving her both course familiarity and stamina credentials; her STYLE_FIT flag reflects the fact she is operating slightly out of typical role in a race where she will go forward — here, however, going forward is the natural thing to do and it suits her entirely.

runners_data.name: Mystic Rose
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up mare for Patrick Magee with headgear (t), placed over 12f on soft, but her two runs on good going include a 5th at 13f and a 7th at 16f — the trip should suit but she has yet to convert in these conditions.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: The field's most viable prominent type behind Jurality, with course form including a 3rd over 18f on good and another place over 14f on soft; Adam Grant's apprentice allowance is taken by Joseph Harnett so Sadhbh Tormey rides, and Maxwell Smart's ability to sit close to the pace is the key tactical weapon here.

runners_data.name: Voice Of Northeast
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Terence O'Brien who carries a repeated fading-in-finish flag — his best recent form came at 13f on good (4th) but an 8-runner sample over 8f on various surfaces suggests he has drifted in trip; being pushed into an unnatural midfield map position further reduces confidence in his ability to deliver.

runners_data.name: Numidia
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old for Peter Lawlor who wears a visor and is a natural rear-sitting type, yet with seven hold-up types in the field he cannot realistically occupy his preferred position; recent form shows a 4th over 16f at Southwell and otherwise low-teens finishes, limiting expectations significantly.

runners_data.name: Al What
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's four-year-old carries a fades-in-finish warning and has failed to place in five runs including a 14th over 12f on good recently — his natural style is hold-up and with the map placing him in midfield against his instincts, the profile is unflattering.

runners_data.name: Celestially
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's three-year-old is lightly weighted on 126lbs and has placed over 12f on good, the best piece of relevant form in her CV, though fades-in-finish is a repeated concern; headgear (p) suggests she needs restraining, and stepping up markedly in trip to 13f+ is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Miners Cabin
runners_data.note: Modest record for Kevin Coleman with five consecutive low finishes including 13th at 16f on good and 12th at 13f — a natural hold-up horse whose natural position is blocked by the field's density of similar types, and the fades-in-finish flag compounds the difficulty.

runners_data.name: Velvet And Vine
runners_data.note: Jennifer Lynch's six-year-old wears a hood (p) and was placed over 12f at Southwell on standard, showing some stamina; her best Bellewstown run was 10th over 16f on good, so the trip and course are familiar but results have been modest — a genuine rear-sitter who cannot access that position freely here.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: Liam McAteer's six-year-old has faded in finish across recent starts and his last five runs over 8-13f on good or standard have produced finishes of 6th through 14th; another natural hold-up type displaced from the back of the field, and trip experience beyond a mile is limited based on recent routing.

races.paceDynamic: Jurality is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field at 1m6½f on good ground at Bellewstown, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate a measured, uncontested gallop from the front. Maxwell Smart is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and may track Jurality into second position, but the bulk of this field — Kevin The Great, Desert Friend, Mystic Rose, Voice Of Northeast, Numidia, Al What, Celestially, Miners Cabin, Velvet And Vine, and Bang Po — are natural hold-up types, creating an unusually back-heavy shape that leaves Jurality almost entirely free to control tempo. The field holds significantly more hold-up and rear-sitting types than the race map can accommodate at the back, meaning Voice Of Northeast, Numidia, Al What, Miners Cabin, Velvet And Vine, and Bang Po will not all get their true running position; Maxwell Smart and, if he travels well enough, Kevin The Great are likeliest to press forward and occupy the midfield slots. At 1m6½f on a fair surface with only one pace-setter dictating a sustainable rhythm, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently just behind Jurality and then sustain their effort in the straight — true hold-up finishers face a searching task if they are stuck in traffic and unable to close quickly enough on a horse that has never been asked to quicken from a pressured pace.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Storm Home

scenarios.body: If Jurality sets an unusually fast pace for the grade that causes the race to collapse in the final furlong, opening the door for back-markers.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Jurality goes too slow and the race becomes a slow-run bunch sprint in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Jurality goes too slow and the race becomes a slow-run bunch sprint in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Jurality — watch whether Adam Grant allows her to stride on freely from the jump or is restrained early; if she is allowed to bowl along uncontested she controls the pace entirely and the outcome of most scenarios hinges on whether anything can catch her.

Maxwell Smart — the only horse with genuine prominent credentials to challenge Jurality; if Sadhbh Tormey positions him smoothly in second in the early stages watch him closely from the 3f pole as he is the most likely beneficiary if Jurality is caught.

Kevin The Great — Gavin Cromwell's runner has form over this course and trip in good going and is capable of a bold late run, but watch the early stages to see if Joseph Harnett rides him closer than his usual hold-up style — a more prominent ride than expected would significantly elevate his chance.

Voice Of Northeast and Al What — both carry fades-in-finish flags and are mapped into midfield against their natural hold-up style; if either drifts back to the rear in the early stages and the pace is moderate, watch whether they make any meaningful ground through the final two furlongs or confirm the fading trend.

Desert Friend — the veteran's win came on soft ground over 14f and Conor Cusack rides; watch whether he travels with any fluency in the first half of the race, as his good-ground form has been poor and any scrimmaging early in a 12-runner field could cost him the stamina reserve he needs at this trip.

runners_data.name: Lark In The Mornin
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with course form, a 39-day turnaround after a winning sequence of 1-1 at 12f and 14f on Good, and a booking for top amateur Mr P W Mullins; suits tracking the pace and challenging late, and the similar-going record (8 runs, 2W 3P) is encouraging for today's conditions.

runners_data.name: The Mediator
runners_data.note: Three consecutive placings including a recent third on Good give Gordon Elliott's nine-year-old solid each-way claims on form, though it is a natural front-runner by inclination — squeezed back by the race shape into a midfield role it doesn't seek, which tempers its prospects of landing this from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Can Happen
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR 120 alongside Intense Approach, with a course-and-distance win on Good in its recent history; stepping back sharply in trip from 16f+ assignments and ridden by a 7lb claimer, but the class edge over most rivals is real if the trip is not an issue.

runners_data.name: Intense Approach
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter, OR 120, and clearly able at this level — but the 112-day jumps absence is a material flag, and a headgear-free prominent style tag with a STYLE_FIT note means its ability to convert front-running control into a winning margin is not guaranteed; John McConnell has had moderate recent strike rate.

runners_data.name: Swelltime
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type with a formal fade warning, returning from 320 days off (35 days since a hurdles run); most recent form reads 8-9-10 and this trip on Good is well within range, but current ability looks well below what this field requires.

runners_data.name: Talking Tough
runners_data.note: OR 34 and winless in 15 runs, with the form string showing consistent tail-end finishes; naturally a hold-up runner but displaced even further back by redistribution, carries a headgear note (blinkers/pads) and a fade warning, and the 12-day turnaround does little to change a bleak picture.

runners_data.name: Weston
runners_data.note: Amateur-ridden hold-up type with a fade flag, last seen 94 days ago; showed a placed effort over 12f on Good and has some ability on this surface, but the OR 79 and a tendency to fade home suggest it needs a pace collapse rather than a controlled front-running scenario to get involved.

races.paceDynamic: Intense Approach is the confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, is the only horse likely to bowl along unchallenged at the head of affairs over this 1m4½f trip on Good ground at Bellewstown. With just seven runners and no genuine pace rival prepared to contest the lead, Intense Approach should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a lung-busting test — conditions that suit a horse who can get loose in front and maintain rhythm. Lark In The Mornin and Can Happen are both prominent-style runners who will want to sit close, but neither profiles as a natural front-runner who will take Intense Approach on. The field does hold more prominent-to-midfield types than the race shape can neatly accommodate — The Mediator and Talking Tough are genuine prominent/hold-up runners respectively who are mapped off their natural positions, meaning both face compromised roles. This race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can track or challenge the pace through the final bend and quicken in the straight, with pure hold-up horses at a meaningful structural disadvantage against a steady-to-fair tempo.

watchPoints.text: Intense Approach's 112-day absence is the single biggest threat to Scenario A — watch to see if it settles fluently in front or shows signs of rustiness/weakness in the straight that allow Lark In The Mornin to sweep past.

Can Happen steps back from 16f+ to 1m4½f today — watch whether it travels comfortably in the prominent group early; if it struggles to hold its position against Intense Approach's pace, its OR 120 class advantage may not materialise.

The Mediator is a natural front-runner posted in a midfield slot purely by virtue of the race shape — if it pushes forward regardless and attempts to challenge Intense Approach for the lead, the pace dynamic changes materially and the entire shape could quicken earlier than expected.

Bellewstown's 1m4½f course is tight and undulating — watch the field position rounding the final bend; prominent horses who secure a clean run from the rail position will have a structural advantage over any hold-up horse needing to find space in a small field.

Three of the seven jockeys carry 7lb claims (Benson, Byrne, Ryan) — in a race where small positional errors could be costly over this trip, watch for any rough passages in running that expose the less experienced riders aboard Can Happen, Intense Approach, and Talking Tough.
